h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר נ״ד Pesach — Maamar Nun Daled
Acharon shel Pesach and the Future Redemption; Pesach as Head of the Festivals; Pidyon HaBen

p: I saw from a certain holy Rav
שֶׁכָּתַב הַטַּעַם שֶׁנִּקְרָא אַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח
who wrote the reason it is called Acharon shel Pesach, the Last of Pesach:
that it alludes to the Pesach of the future,
and also that even the lowliest in Yisrael
but he did not explain the reason.
That is, it was difficult for him
לָמָּה נִקְרָא כֵּן בְּפִי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
why it is so called by all Yisrael,
and presumably there is a reason for it.
On the simple level it is understood:
דְּכָל יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל גָּלוּיוֹת
every second festival day of the Diaspora
is called like the first festival day.
לֹא יוּכְלוּ לִקְרוֹת לְיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל גָּלוּיוֹת
one cannot call the second festival day of the Diaspora
“Shemini Atzeres,” the Eighth Day, since it is the ninth;
but then there is something new,
and it is called Simchas Torah.
That is not so on Pesach:
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִקְרוֹת הַיּוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל גָּלוּיוֹת
one cannot call the second festival day of the Diaspora
שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל פֶּסַח שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא שְׁמִינִי
“Shevi'i shel Pesach,” the Seventh of Pesach, since it is the eighth,
so we call it Acharon shel Pesach.
But nevertheless the reason he wrote
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶׁמּוּבָא בְּתִיקּוּנֵי זוֹהַר
It is based on what is brought in the Tikkunei Zohar
“that they will be erased with yud-daled (fourteen)—
דְּאִינּוּן אַרְבַּע סְרֵי יוֹמֵי דְּפִסְחָא וְכוּלֵּי
which are the fourteen days of Pesach, etc.,
and this is the seven days of Pesach
and the seven days of Pesach
We have already said that the future redemption
and of this it is said (Michah 7:15):
“As in the days of your going out of the land of Egypt
“I will show him” is written in the hidden third person,
And the last day of Pesach will be
the first day of the seven days of Pesach
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז לְפֶסַח שֶׁל עָתִיד.
That is what they meant: it alludes to the Pesach of the future.
And this is also the intent
that even the last of Yisrael
will have a share in it.
For then it will become clear that “Your people are all righteous”:
everyone who is of the seed of Yaakov
For this is the purpose of the whole length of the exile:
“so that no one banished be cast away from Him,”
and “the lost will come, etc., and the banished, etc.”:
who were assimilated among the nations, Heaven forbid,
and even those banished in desires,
which the kelipah of Egypt signifies—
in them too the great shofar will awaken,
a stirring of teshuvah in the heart
after seven days have passed in vigilance
against the slightest chametz and leaven,
which are the kelipah of the Sitra Achra and its female counterpart,
even the lowliest and last in Yisrael
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרֵךְ עוֹמֵד עַל הַפֶּתַח
which alludes that Hashem, blessed be He, stands at the doorway
so that the evil inclination not accuse them,
and especially when it falls on Shabbos,
“He who guards the Shabbos from profaning it
and guards his hand from doing any evil”:
as they said in the Mechilta (Beshalach, Vayisa 5),
and in Pri Etz Chaim the wording is
that one is saved from the accusation of the evil inclination.
to be redeemed on this Pesach
and to merit the Pesach of the future to come,

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Naftali Tzvi of Ropshitz, Zera Kodesh, Acharon shel Pesach — “After the Seventh of Pesach, when we read in the Torah the Song they sang over the miracle of the going out of Egypt, we keep Acharon shel Pesach, and through the Song we allude to the miracle of the future; therefore we read as haftarah on this day ‘Today he will halt at Nov,’ where the whole matter of the redemption to come is written. This is ‘Az’ (whose numerical value is eight): on the last day of Pesach, the eighth day, we allude to the future redemption. Therefore it is written ‘yashir,’ ‘will sing,’ and not ‘sang,’ for the eight alludes to the redemption to come, when they will reach the eighth attribute, the attribute of Binah, the world of freedom.” Connection: Like Rav Tzadok, the Ropshitzer reads the last day of Pesach as the start of the future Pesach rooted in Binah; he adds the textual sign of the eighth day in the Song and the haftarah.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach II, Korach — “‘And the lost in the land of Ashur and the banished in the land of Egypt will come.’ ‘Lost’ is one whose body appears clean, and only in the root of his soul is there a lack that is barely noticeable, like Korach; he is lost entirely, for he cannot arrive at his lack, since in his own eyes he is pure. But in the future, when Hashem reveals to him the difference between him and Moshe, he will turn in a moment from darkness to light. The ‘banished’ is one whose body is distant and sunk in the evil inclination, and it is very hard to refine him; therefore the lost precede the banished in teshuvah.” Connection: Both read Yeshayah’s lost and banished as kinds of souls the great shofar will bring back, with the banished in Egypt as those sunk in desire; the Izhbitzer adds that the lost are the outwardly clean.

p: “The festival in it is the new year for festivals.”
“Head” indicates that it is the head,
and the body follows the head
and all the holiness of the festivals
branches out from the Chag of Pesach.
That is: after a Jew has been careful
all the festival against the slightest chametz and leaven,
which allude to the evil inclination,
and counts the days of the Sefirah
זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי זֶה אַחַר כָּךְ בְּכָל שָׁנָה
through this one merits afterwards each year
that it be as it was then:
for the first blemish has already been repaired.
And then it is permitted to offer leaven to the Most High,
meaning that the leaven is only
“that of which a little is good” (Berachos 34a),
and it is what will remain of the evil inclination
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא (מִדְרָשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם חֵלֶק א קל"ח.)
as is brought (Midrash HaNe'elam, Zohar I 138a):
“Were it not for the evil inclination,
there would be no joy of Torah learning”;
שֶׁלְּתַכְלִית זֶה בָּרָא ה' יִתְבָּרֵךְ הַיֵּצֶר הָרַע
for this purpose Hashem, blessed be He, created the evil inclination,
I created the Torah as its spice,”
so that the longing be drawn
to be a desire for Torah.
וְכָל מִי שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל תּוֹרָה
“And whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah,
the yoke of government is removed from him
and the yoke of worldly occupation” (Avos 3:5).
the holiness of the Chag of Sukkos,
to dwell in the shade of faith,
so that his heart be the holiness of the camp of Yisrael
as it was in the wilderness,
surrounded by the Clouds of Glory,
and Hashem, blessed be He, will dwell in his heart,
like one who attains the supernal Shabbos,
as stated in the Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 48):
זַכָּאָה מַאן דַּעֲבִיד לוֹן דִּירָה בְּשַׁבָּת
“Fortunate is he who makes for them a dwelling on Shabbos
in the two chambers of the heart,
and the evil inclination clears out from there, etc.”;
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַפֶּסַח
and this too comes through the holiness of Pesach,
that one was careful against the slightest chametz and leaven.
which is the wellspring of Torah,
namely as it was with the First Tablets,
שֶׁהָיָה כָּלוּל כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
in which the entire Oral Torah was included
כְּמוֹ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
like the Oral Torah of Moshe Rabbeinu,
explicitly from Hashem, blessed be He
And all of this branches out
from the holiness of the Chag of Pesach, as was said.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 4a — "'For the festivals': the festivals — on the first of Nissan? They are on the fifteenth of Nissan! Rav Chisda said: The festival that falls in it [Nissan] is the new year for the festivals." Rashi: the festival in it — the festival that falls in the month whose first day is the new year; i.e., Pesach.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tiferes Yosef, Shavuos — “Chametz was forbidden in the Temple, for chametz denotes human grasp and human action: it grows through human action and the passing of time, so one may imagine ‘my strength and the might of my hand made me this wealth.’ The two loaves of Atzeres are different, for it says ‘and you shall count for yourselves seven weeks’: a person refines himself so much in the forty-nine days of the count, refined sevenfold, that he stands with his grasp close to Hashem; then it is permitted to bring chametz to the Temple, for Hashem shows him that his grasp too has a place.” Connection: Both make the sevenfold refining of the Omer what permits leaven on Shavuos; for the Izhbitzer the leaven is human grasp and effort, which after the count is shown to have a place before Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharal, Derush al HaTorah — “This is the matter of the two loaves that came with the lambs of Atzeres as chametz. Why did these alone, of all offerings, come as chametz? The reason is that chametz is the evil inclination, the leaven in the dough that holds one back, which a person must truly keep far as long as there is any concern in the world that it may bring him to sin. But when there is no concern at all, there is no need to keep it far. Therefore Hashem commanded to offer chametz, which is the evil inclination, on Atzeres, the day of the Giving of the Torah and on no other, for the Torah does not let it rule over a person.” Connection: Maharal gives the same reading of the Shavuos leaven as an evil inclination no longer to be feared; he grounds the permission in the Torah’s power over the inclination, where Rav Tzadok grounds it in the refinement of Pesach and the Omer.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 5 — “At the Giving of the Torah it is written ‘I said, you are angels,’ for every blemish of the serpent was repaired and the evil inclination was nullified. Though after the corruption it returned to its place, every year when this time comes its holiness is aroused, the nullification of the leaven in the dough; what remains is only the leaven ‘whose majority is harsh and whose minority is good,’ what is needed and will remain even in the future, as in ‘were it not for the evil inclination there would be no joy of Torah learning.’ Therefore on this day leaven is offered, the good minority that remained.” Connection: The same chain from Sinai through ‘a little is good’ to the leaven of Shavuos; it adds that therefore all agree that on Atzeres bodily enjoyment, ‘for you,’ can also be holy.

p: אֲשֶׁר פָּסַח עַל בָּתֵּי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִצְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר
“who passed over the houses of the Children of Yisrael in Egypt,” etc.;
and this was said to them in Egypt.
(פְּרִי צַדִּיק חֵלֶק ב מַאֲמָר א' דְּפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן)
“Rabbi Simlai happened to a pidyon haben,”
which has no connection to what precedes it.
But this is the essence of the holiness of Pesach:
that a fixed holiness remains from it in the firstborn.
And the redemption is from a Kohen,
for the Kohen is the agent of the Merciful One,
and the holiness remains with the Kohen.
That is why they were in doubt
certainly they would not have been in doubt
about reciting Shehecheyanu over a monetary gain,
for we find it only with new vessels
not with monetary gain to put away in a box;
when he buys something, then he will bless.
But the Kohen, through the redemption,
takes the holiness from the firstborn.
and this refers to the day after the festival
meaning that the holiness of the festival remains,
and the holiness of Pesach is the sanctification of the firstborn.
And in the passage of “Sanctify” the mitzvah of tefillin is written,
which seems to have no connection,
and was not needed for that hour,
שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא הָיָה עוֹד פָּרָשַׁת שְׁמַע וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמוֹעַ
for the passages of Shema and Vehayah Im Shamoa did not yet exist
for the sanctification of the firstborn
is the holiness of the Oral Torah.
“For the lips of the Kohen guard knowledge,
and they seek Torah from his mouth.”
And the essence of the holiness of Pesach is
אֲשֶׁר פָּסַח עַל בָּתֵּי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
“who passed over the houses of the Children of Yisrael”
“and will not allow the destroyer to enter,” etc.:
he is the evil inclination (Bava Basra 16a).
That is, since it became clear
that they are bound at the root—
and this is the root of the holiness of the firstborn.
And the essence of the Oral Torah
is from the dew of Atika,
וְהַיְינוּ טַל שֶׁעָתִיד לְהַחֲיוֹת בּוֹ הַמֵּתִים
meaning the dew with which He will revive the dead
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ כָּל הָעוֹסֵק בְּטַל תּוֹרָה
That is what they said: “Whoever engages in the dew of Torah,
the dew of Torah revives him”
(as brought in the Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 19,
And after the redemption, the Kohen attains this.
Likewise regarding tefillin it is written (Shemos 13:9):
לְמַעַן תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת ה' בְּפִיךָ וְגוֹמֵר
“So that the Torah of Hashem be in your mouth,” etc.—
“My words that I have placed in your mouth,”
Therefore the mitzvah of tefillin was written
in the passage of the sanctification of the firstborn.
And this is the root of the holiness of Pesach:
that through the plague of the firstborn they attained
and afterwards at the splitting of the Sea;
וְלֹא יִתֵּן הַמַּשְׁחִית לָבוֹא אֶל בָּתֵּיכֶם
“and He will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses”—
so that the evil inclination cannot enter.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Arizal, Shaar HaKavanos, Derushei Isru Chag 3 — “Why is there an Isru Chag after a festival and not after Shabbos? The weekdays are the secret of Yetzirah and below. On Shabbos, Yetzirah and Asiyah, the secret of the weekdays, rise to the place of complete holiness, the world of Atzilus; therefore at its departure they become entirely weekday again and have no power to retain the light of Atzilus. But on a festival, Yetzirah and Asiyah did not rise to Atzilus; the supernal light was drawn to them while they stood below, so after the festival, in the plain weekday, a little of that diminished light can remain in them. This is ‘Bind the festival with cords’: bind and tie the light of the festival so that it remain in existence after the festival.” Connection: The Arizal gives the Kabbalistic mechanism for the principle Rav Tzadok draws from the same verse, that a festival leaves holiness behind it; Rav Tzadok locates Pesach’s remnant in the firstborn.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Leil Rishon shel Pesach 44 — “Israel are called firstborn, as it is written ‘My son, My firstborn, Israel,’ on account of the beginning of thought, for Israel arose in thought, and thought, Chochmah, is called firstborn. On this it is said ‘Sanctify to Me every firstborn’: Hashem sanctified the primordial thought in which Israel arose first. The thought of Israel is always bound to the root of the supernal will, but this point is greatly hidden because of the leaven in the dough, which conceals this bond. Therefore it is said ‘Sanctify to Me every firstborn’: a person should rouse his deeds and strip the leaven from them, and then this point will be revealed in them.” Connection: Both make the firstborn’s holiness Israel’s bond at the root, which overcomes the evil inclination; Sod Yesharim adds that the leaven hides the bond, so stripping it reveals the firstborn point.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 88b — "With every utterance that came from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed is He, the souls of Israel departed… Since their souls departed at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will revive the dead in the future and revived them, as it is said, 'A generous rain You shed, O God.'" Rashi: 'generous rain' — written in Tehillim regarding the Giving of the Torah.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pidyon HaBen 2 — “At the tenth plague Israel were clarified as bound at the root, ‘My son, My firstborn, Israel.’ In the passages of Shema it is written ‘and you shall bind,’ but here, in the passage of ‘Sanctify,’ it is written ‘and it shall be,’ for these passages were said before the Giving of the Torah, when everything was from Hashem’s side. And here it is written ‘a remembrance between your eyes’ and not ‘frontlets,’ a crown: he will merit only a remembrance, for the evil inclination makes one forget; that is, the removal of the leaven in the dough, and through this ‘so that the Torah of Hashem be in your mouth.’” Connection: The same link between tefillin in the passage of the firstborn and the firstborn bound at the root; it adds the contrast of ‘remembrance’ here with ‘frontlets’ in the Shema passages.
